implemented: legacy/compat list constructs are classified honestly instead of reported as Loss: {\*\listtext ...}/{\listtext ...}/{\pntext ...} are the cached list text regenerated from the list table (dropping them avoids a double marker), {\*\levelmarker ...} is a legacy alternative marker superseded by \leveltext, and \jclisttab/\levelspace/\levelindent/\leveltemplateid/\levelold/\fbias are Word 6/7 list-level compatibility markers with no Strict equivalent. Corpus import losses fall by 8798 across the affected documents.

the list table already maps \list/\listid/\listlevel/\levelnfc/\levelnfcn/\levelstartat/\leveljc/\leveljcn/\levelfollow/\leveltext -> w:abstractNum/w:lvl (start, numFmt, lvlText, lvlJc, suff) and \listoverride/\listid/\ls -> w:num; negative \listid is preserved as an unsigned source identity.

list override levels are mapped: {\lfolevel ...} (with or without the \* prefix) now builds a w:lvlOverride on the w:num. {\listoverrideformat{\listlevel ...}} routes the nested level controls through the same helper as the w:abstractNum levels and stores the replacement as LevelOverride.level; {\listoverridestart\levelstartatN} stores LevelOverride.start_override without a w:lvl. The level index is the \lfolevel ordinal (0-based, up to nine); \listoverridecount accepts any value (it is redundant with the groups actually present). Corpus 021 now carries w:lvlOverride (the bullet glyph replacing the abstract '*' marker): import losses 152 -> 131 under the RC0506 options, and three \list:unbound-text events disappear because the nested characters are consumed by the level-text destination.

\levelold (Word 6/7 conversion marker) and \fbias (the East-Asian font-bias hint Word emits only inside a \listlevel, with no direct w:rFonts analogue) join the list-compat Info set, so they no longer mask real losses.
remaining: counter continuity across paragraphs/tables/sections is a renderer concern and was not re-audited here.
list:unbound-text (text directly inside listtable/listoverridetable) stays a Loss; it is malformed source, not a supported construct.

the 2026-10-11 full-corpus WPS run surfaces one oracle text quirk unrelated to lists: 014's `\flddirty` PAGEREF keeps the RTF's stale cached page number while WPS recomputes it on export (see corpus_gates). Pagination 65/100 and pixels 6/100 reflect the RC02/RC03/RC04 face-fidelity gap, not RC05.
